proposal.utterance: A contract is a generically dependent continuant encoding mutual obligations.

entities.label: Contract
entities.rationale: A contract is a kind of generically dependent continuant: its content (the encoded obligations) is an information artifact that can be instantiated in multiple physical carriers (paper copies, digital files) while remaining the same contract. This matches BFO_0000031 precisely.

entities.label: MutualObligation
entities.rationale: A mutual obligation is a bilateral legal obligation — a role borne by each party to a contract with respect to the other. It is a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation (which is already typed as BFO_0000023 Role). The 'mutual' qualifier marks that two parties each bear a correlative obligation role simultaneously.

relations.rationale: Establishes Contract as a subclass of Generically dependent continuant per the utterance.
MutualObligation is a specialisation of the existing LegalObligation class; bilateral structure is the differentiating characteristic.
Placeholder relation capturing 'encodes mutual obligations'; see open_questions for refinement.

open_questions: Should the 'encodes mutual obligations' relationship be modelled as an OWL existential restriction (working:Contract rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000051 some working:MutualObligation) rather than a plain subClassOf, to avoid the implication that every Contract IS a MutualObligation? The has-part relation between a GDC and its encoded content-parts needs care.

Is 'mutual' intended to mean that both parties bear identical obligation types, or merely that each bears some obligation toward the other (which may differ)? This affects whether MutualObligation should be a single role class or modelled as two correlated role instances.
Should working:Contract also be linked to working:LegalForm or working:LegalArchitecture as a broader institutional-document class?
Should individual contracts (e.g., a specific signed agreement) also be representable as individuals of type working:Contract, or is only the class needed at this stage?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance introduces two new ontological commitments: (1) Contract as a class of generically dependent continuants (BFO_0000031), justified because contracts are information artifacts whose content is substrate-independent; and (2) MutualObligation as a subclass of the existing LegalObligation role class, capturing the bilateral normative structure the utterance attributes to contracts. The utterance further claims that contracts 'encode' mutual obligations, which in BFO terms is most precisely an existential parthood or concretization relation between the GDC (contract content) and the role instances (obligations) it specifies — but since BFO_0000031 items do not straightforwardly 'have parts' in the mereological sense, this relation is flagged as an open question rather than committed as a plain subClassOf. The plain subClassOf from Contract to MutualObligation is included as a conservative placeholder pending user confirmation of the preferred axiom form.

proposal.utterance: Offer and acceptance are phases of contract formation.

entities.label: ContractFormation
entities.rationale: Contract formation is a process that unfolds in time, during which a contract comes into being. It is typed as a BFO Process (BFO_0000015).

entities.label: Offer
entities.rationale: An offer is a phase or subprocess of contract formation — a temporally bounded process in which a proposing party communicates terms to another. Typed as BFO Process (BFO_0000015), as it is an occurrent happening.

entities.label: Acceptance
entities.rationale: Acceptance is a phase of contract formation — a temporally bounded process in which the offeree communicates agreement to terms. Typed as BFO Process (BFO_0000015).

relations.rationale: The utterance asserts Offer is a phase of ContractFormation. In BFO, a phase of a process is a process part; subclassing under ContractFormation here captures that every instance of Offer is a part of some ContractFormation process. A more precise relation would be BFO_0000050 (part of) at the instance level, but at the class level we use subClassOf with the intent that Offer instances are process parts of ContractFormation instances.

ContractFormation has part Offer — expresses at the class level that contract formation processes include offer phases as parts (BFO_0000051 has part).
ContractFormation has part Acceptance — expresses at the class level that contract formation processes include acceptance phases as parts (BFO_0000051 has part).

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that Offer and Acceptance are phases of ContractFormation, all of which are new to the ontology. All three are typed as BFO Processes (BFO_0000015) because they are occurrents that unfold in time. The phase relationship is captured by (a) subClassOf from Offer and Acceptance to ContractFormation — indicating that instances of these classes are also instances of ContractFormation in a parthood sense — and (b) BFO_0000051 (has part) relations from ContractFormation to Offer and Acceptance at the class level, representing that contract formation processes have offer and acceptance phases as parts. There is a known BFO modeling tension here: 'phase of' is strictly a part-of relation at the instance level (BFO_0000050), not a subtype relation; the open questions flag this for the user to decide whether to use OWL property restrictions (ContractFormation subClassOf (BFO_0000051 some Offer)) instead of or in addition to subClassOf axioms.

entities.label: Consideration
entities.rationale: Consideration in contract law is an internally grounded capacity of a legal act or party — it is the condition that makes a promise legally binding. This fits BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer and is realized in a process.

entities.label: ContractFormationProcess
entities.rationale: The formation of a contract is a process — an occurrent that unfolds in time. The utterance says consideration is realized 'in the formation process', so we need a class for this process as the realization target.

relations.rationale: BFO_0000054 (realized in) links a realizable entity (Disposition) to the process in which it is realized. The utterance directly asserts that consideration is realized in the formation process, so this is the canonical BFO relation to express that claim at the class level.

open_questions: Is 'Consideration' intended as a class (a kind of disposition borne by any contractual party or promise) or as a specific individual instance within a particular legal system or contract?
Should 'ContractFormationProcess' be a subclass of an existing working class, or is it sufficiently distinct to stand alone under BFO_0000015?

Does consideration inhere in the contracting party (a person), in the promise (a generically dependent continuant), or in the contract as a material document? Identifying the bearer is needed for a complete BFO model.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that consideration — a legal concept denoting what makes a promise enforceable — is a disposition that is realized in a contract formation process. In BFO terms, Disposition (BFO_0000016) is the correct type: it is a specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in its bearer and whose manifestation (realization) occurs in a process. The relation BFO_0000054 (realized in) directly expresses the asserted relationship between the disposition and the process. A new class ContractFormationProcess is minted as a subclass of BFO Process (BFO_0000015) to serve as the realization target. Both are introduced as classes rather than individuals because the utterance uses common-noun phrasing ('consideration', 'the formation process') denoting kinds. Open questions remain about the bearer of consideration and the exact scope of 'formation process'.

proposal.utterance: A breach of contract is a process that disrupts the enduring obligation relation.

entities.label: BreachOfContract
entities.rationale: A breach of contract is a kind of happening or event — an occurrent process in which obligations are violated. It unfolds in time and is naturally typed as a BFO Process.

entities.label: ObligationRelationDisruption
entities.rationale: The 'disruption' of an enduring obligation relation is best modeled as a quality that inheres in the LegalObligation (a specifically dependent continuant) and reflects a changed or impaired state. It captures the altered property of the obligation after a breach without conflating the breach event itself with the resultant state.

relations.rationale: BreachOfContract is a subclass of BFO Process, as it is a temporal occurrence involving participants.
ObligationRelationDisruption is a subclass of BFO Quality, representing the disrupted state of the obligation relation that inheres in the bearer.

Instances of ObligationRelationDisruption inhere in instances of LegalObligation; using domain restriction to connect the quality class to its obligatory bearer class. (Note: in full OWL this would be an existential restriction via RO_0000052, but listed here as a subclass with bearer constraint for proposer clarity.)

A breach-of-contract process realizes (or more precisely, participates in altering) the LegalObligation role. Using BFO_0000055 (realizes) to indicate the process brings the obligation's disposition into actuality as a disruption. Open to revision — see open_questions.

open_questions: Should 'disruption of the enduring obligation relation' be modeled as a Quality inhering in LegalObligation, or as a distinct Disposition (capacity to be disrupted) that is realized in the BreachOfContract process?

Is 'enduring obligation relation' intended to refer to an instance of the existing working:LegalObligation class, or does it refer to a broader relational structure (e.g., working:RelationalDependencyNetwork or working:EnduringInstitutionalForm)?
Should BreachOfContract be typed as a subclass of working:BehavioralLegalManifestation (already a Process subclass) rather than directly under BFO Process, given the existing hierarchy?

The relation BFO_0000055 (realizes) connects a process to a realizable entity (Role or Disposition), not to a Quality. If disruption is modeled as a Quality, a different predicate (e.g., a custom 'results in' or 'causes') may be needed — shall we mint that relation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two ontological commitments: (1) that a breach of contract is a Process (BFO_0000015), and (2) that such a process disrupts an 'enduring obligation relation.' The breach is straightforwardly a BFO Process. The disruption of the obligation relation is trickier: the obligation itself is already modeled as working:LegalObligation (a Role, BFO_0000023), and 'disruption' connotes a change of state in that obligation, which fits best as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in the LegalObligation bearer. The relation between the BreachOfContract process and the LegalObligation is proposed using BFO_0000055 (realizes), though this is questionable because realizes connects processes to realizable entities, not qualities — this is flagged as an open question. The existing class working:BehavioralLegalManifestation (a Process subclass) is a candidate parent for BreachOfContract, but it is not assumed without user confirmation.

proposal.utterance: Specific performance is a remedy-process restoring the obligation's realization.

entities.label: SpecificPerformance
entities.rationale: Specific performance is a type of legal remedy that unfolds in time as a judicial-enforcement process compelling a party to fulfill a contractual obligation. It is a process (BFO_0000015), not merely an abstract information artifact.

entities.label: RemedyProcess
entities.rationale: A remedy-process is a superclass for legal remedy proceedings that occur in time. SpecificPerformance is a subclass of RemedyProcess.

entities.label: ObligationRealization
entities.rationale: The realization of an obligation is the process in which a LegalObligation (a realizable role) is realized — i.e., the bearer performs the required act. BFO_0000054 (realized in) links the obligation-as-realizable to this process. This is the target state that specific performance aims to restore.

relations.rationale: Specific performance is a species of remedy-process.
Both SpecificPerformance and RemedyProcess are processes (BFO_0000015), unfolding in time.
RemedyProcess is a subclass of BFO Process.
ObligationRealization is the process in which a LegalObligation is realized; it is a BFO Process.
BFO_0000054 (realized in): LegalObligation as a realizable entity is realized in the ObligationRealization process. This captures the core BFO semantics of disposition/role realization.

The utterance states that specific performance restores the obligation's realization; modeled as specific performance being a subclass of ObligationRealization (the process that realizes the obligation), encoding that specific performance is the court-compelled instantiation of that realization.

open_questions: Should SpecificPerformance be modeled strictly as a subclass of ObligationRealization, or as a distinct RemedyProcess that *causes* or *has part* an ObligationRealization? The 'restoring' language may imply a causal/enabling relation rather than identity of process type.
Is the LegalObligation being realized here a contractual obligation specifically? If so, should we introduce a ContractualObligation subclass of LegalObligation?
Should SpecificPerformance also be linked to a CourtAuthority role (existing individual) via RO_0000057 (has participant), since it is court-ordered?
Does 'restoring' imply a prior process of breach (a process of non-realization) that specific performance corrects? Should we model a BreachOfObligation process class as well?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that specific performance is a remedy-process that restores the realization of an obligation. In BFO terms, a LegalObligation is already in the working ontology as a realizable entity (role, BFO_0000023). Its realization is a process (BFO_0000015) linked via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Specific performance is itself a process — a judicial-enforcement happening unfolding in time — and is typed as a subclass of a newly minted RemedyProcess class (itself a BFO Process), which is in turn related to ObligationRealization. The 'restoring' language is captured by making SpecificPerformance a subclass of ObligationRealization, meaning that in a specific-performance proceeding the obligation's realization is (re-)instantiated. Three new classes are proposed: RemedyProcess, SpecificPerformance, and ObligationRealization, all under BFO_0000015. entities.label: SpecificPerformance
entities.rationale: Specific performance is a type of legal remedy that unfolds in time as a judicial-enforcement process compelling a party to fulfill a contractual obligation. It is a process (BFO_0000015), not merely an abstract information artifact.

entities.label: RemedyProcess
entities.rationale: A remedy-process is a superclass for legal remedy proceedings that occur in time. SpecificPerformance is a subclass of RemedyProcess.

entities.label: ObligationRealization
entities.rationale: The realization of an obligation is the process in which a LegalObligation (a realizable role) is realized — i.e., the bearer performs the required act. BFO_0000054 (realized in) links the obligation-as-realizable to this process. This is the target state that specific performance aims to restore.

relations.rationale: Specific performance is a species of remedy-process.
Both SpecificPerformance and RemedyProcess are processes (BFO_0000015), unfolding in time.
RemedyProcess is a subclass of BFO Process.
ObligationRealization is the process in which a LegalObligation is realized; it is a BFO Process.
BFO_0000054 (realized in): LegalObligation as a realizable entity is realized in the ObligationRealization process. This captures the core BFO semantics of disposition/role realization.

The utterance states that specific performance restores the obligation's realization; modeled as specific performance being a subclass of ObligationRealization (the process that realizes the obligation), encoding that specific performance is the court-compelled instantiation of that realization.

Should SpecificPerformance also be linked to a CourtAuthority role (existing individual) via RO_0000057 (has participant), since it is court-ordered?
Does 'restoring' imply a prior process of breach (a process of non-realization) that specific performance corrects? Should we model a BreachOfObligation process class as well?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that specific performance is a remedy-process that restores the realization of an obligation. In BFO terms, a LegalObligation is already in the working ontology as a realizable entity (role, BFO_0000023). Its realization is a process (BFO_0000015) linked via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Specific performance is itself a process — a judicial-enforcement happening unfolding in time — and is typed as a subclass of a newly minted RemedyProcess class (itself a BFO Process), which is in turn related to ObligationRealization. The 'restoring' language is captured by making SpecificPerformance a subclass of ObligationRealization, meaning that in a specific-performance proceeding the obligation's realization is (re-)instantiated. Three new classes are proposed: RemedyProcess, SpecificPerformance, and ObligationRealization, all under BFO_0000015.
